name: Socialism of the 21st century
summary: Socialism of the 21st century is a Latin American left project, first theorized by Heinz Dieterich and put into practice by Chavez, Correa and Morales, that rejects both neoliberal capitalism and Soviet-style state socialism. It combines nationalization of strategic resources, oil-funded social programs, cooperatives and co-management, and participatory democracy through referendums and communal councils, with regional anti-US integration and, in the Andean constitutions, buen vivir, rights of nature and indigenous rights. Change is meant to come gradually through elections and constituent assemblies, with markets and private firms persisting alongside social property.
scope: The Pink Tide strand of the 2000s and 2010s: Dieterich's equivalence economy and participatory democracy, Chavez's Bolivarian turn to socialism from 2005, and the Ecuadorian 2008 constitution of Correa and Bolivia under Morales. It excludes the Chavismo-specific Maduro era, Marxist-Leninist one-party models and moderate social-democratic Pink Tide governments such as Bachelet or Lula.

keyFigures.name: Heinz Dieterich
keyFigures.role: German sociologist who coined and theorized the concept from 1996.

keyFigures.name: Hugo Chávez
keyFigures.role: Venezuelan president who announced socialism of the 21st century in 2005.

keyFigures.name: Rafael Correa
keyFigures.role: Ecuadorian president whose government adopted buen vivir in the 2008 constitution.

sources.title: Socialism of the 21st century
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Origins, Dieterich's equivalence economy and participatory democracy, post-neoliberal policy, ALBA, buen vivir, criticisms.

sources.title: The Meaning of 21st Century Socialism for Venezuela
sources.author: Gregory Wilpert (ZNet, 2006)
sources.usedFor: Property forms, co-management, markets, participation, missions, comparison with state socialism.

sources.title: Constitution of Ecuador (2008)
sources.author: Constitute Project
sources.usedFor: Buen vivir, rights of nature, social function of property, health rights, secular state, indigenous rights, recall.

sources.title: Defying U.S., Venezuela's Chavez Embraces Socialism
sources.author: Pascal Fletcher, Reuters (reprinted in Socialist ViewPoint, March 2005)
sources.usedFor: Chavez's 2005 statements: invent socialism of the 21st century, capitalism cannot solve problems, opposition to US wars.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Free state health care is a flagship of the Bolivarian missions and Ecuador's constitution makes health a state-guaranteed right with universality as a principle.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Post-neoliberal governments expanded welfare and raised incomes of the poor, so substantial minimum-wage increases fit, though the sources do not centre on the wage itself.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Dieterich's model replaces market pricing with value set by those who create it, and Chavez answered that capitalism cannot solve social problems.

public-ownership.rationale: Gas, mining, oil and telecoms were nationalized, but Wilpert notes private ownership still dominates and the aim is a mix with social property.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Redistribution funded the missions, but oil revenue rather than wealth taxes was the main source, so the position is inferred from egalitarian aims.

unions-good.rationale: Workers are meant to take part in co-management and run firms, implying support for organized labor, though the sources say little about unions directly.

property-fundamental.rationale: Ecuador's constitution gives property a social and environmental function and Venezuela expropriated idle factories, so property is subordinate to social aims.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Post-neoliberalism rejects the Washington Consensus and favors heavy state intervention, capital controls and preferential treatment of non-profit-minded firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Expanded welfare and poverty-reduction spending is a defining feature, financed by extractive exports.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperatives and worker takeovers of idle factories were promoted, though Wilpert says co-managed firms will not be fully worker-controlled.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed directly; the humanist, rights-centered constitutions suggest wariness, though security-minded governments differed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Adherent governments split, with Ecuador and Bolivia easing some rules while others kept prohibition, and the sources do not address it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Governments of the strand passed media and anti-discrimination laws, but adherents are divided and the sources are silent on the principle.

strong-leader.rationale: Dieterich and Wilpert stress participatory, libertarian democracy and critics' charges of caudillismo are rejected by adherents, though Chavez himself was a strong executive.

state-harmful.rationale: The model relies on a state as redistributor, planner and owner of strategic industries, and Dieterich speaks of a basic-democratic non-class state, not its abolition.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherent governments differed, so the answer is a genuine split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Chavez integrated the military into civilian tasks, but the sources do not take a stance on more police or military funding and authority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The sources do not address it and adherents are divided between rights-based and abolitionist views.

decide-locally.rationale: Communal councils of 200 to 400 families and local planning councils embody local decision-making, though the national state keeps strategic powers.

rehabilitation.rationale: Ecuador's constitution frames the penal system around rehabilitation, but the sources give little detail, so this is inferred from the humanist outlook.

traditional-family.rationale: The strand is progressive on rights, though adherents such as Correa and Morales were personally conservative on some family issues.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Adherents are split, as Ecuador's 2008 text defined marriage as between a man and a woman while some later left governments in the region accepted it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Left governments of the Pink Tide diverged, with Correa and Chavez opposing liberalization and others supporting it, and the sources do not settle it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ecuador's constitution declares a secular state and secular public education, though adherents are not militantly anti-religious.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Rooted in indigenous movements, it embraces plurinationality, indigenous rights and redress for racial exclusion in Latin America.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources do not discuss the nature of gender, and adherents range from feminist to socially conservative.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The strand values indigenous and popular culture and Bolivarian identity but is mainly regional and plurinational, so views are mixed.

gradual-change.rationale: Dieterich proposes gradual nonviolent transition, but the project aims at deep transformation of institutions rather than respecting established ones.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Regional integration and solidarity with Latin America imply openness; the sources say nothing directly on immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: It favors regional bodies such as ALBA and CELAC that exclude North America and distrusts global institutions seen as run by the IMF and the US.

free-trade.rationale: ALBA was founded explicitly against the US-proposed Free Trade Area of the Americas, and the strand opposes the Washington Consensus.

nation-first.rationale: It prioritizes regional integration and solidarity but also sovereignty against the US, so it rejects both pure nationalism and global cooperation as such.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Chavez condemned the US-led wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, so military intervention abroad is viewed as imperial.

open-borders.rationale: Regional integration points one way and the sources are silent on open borders, so adherents are not clearly aligned.

limit-growth.rationale: Buen vivir criticizes the development model, but the governments pursued extractive growth to fund social programs, so adherents disagree.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Buen vivir and rights of nature favor environmental protection, yet adherent governments relied on oil, so the support is real but inconsistent.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; buen vivir is skeptical of developmentalism while planning envisions technical coordination.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not stated; inferred from the ecological emphasis on buen vivir and rights of nature.

revolution-justified.rationale: Dieterich insists on gradual, nonviolent democratic change, yet Chavez framed his project as a revolution, so adherents are split on the term.

experts-over-public.rationale: The model rests on participatory democracy and referendums, favoring citizen decision over technocratic rule.

central-planning.rationale: Effective economic planning is a stated difference from earlier socialisms, but Wilpert notes markets persist and participatory rather than central planning is stressed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Venezuela kept markets alongside cooperatives, co-managed and state firms, and favored social production enterprises.

land-value-tax.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses a land value tax; it is neither endorsed nor opposed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian redistributive aim, with no source stating a position on inheritance.

basic-income.rationale: Social programs were targeted missions funded by oil, and the sources do not discuss unconditional basic income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Post-neoliberal policy includes protectionism against the Washington Consensus.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Dieterich calls for democratic planning, and oil and nationalized sectors were used to steer development, with capital controls freeing the state from private investors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The model promotes cooperatives and communal property but also state ownership, so wide small-owner distribution is not a defining aim.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Dieterich's equivalence economy keeps value accounting and retains exchange at equivalent labor time, so wages are not simply abolished.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The strand opposes market-led monetary rule and the Washington Consensus, favoring state control and regional currencies like the SUCRE.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Co-management and councils are participatory rather than corporatist, though the sources say nothing on state-set wage bargains.

one-party-rule.rationale: The 1999 constitution enshrines a multi-party system and Dieterich stresses democracy, although critics charge dominant-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: It is a republican, popular-sovereignty tradition rooted in Bolivarian and indigenous democratic ideals.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents stress using democracy itself to gain power, with referendums and basic democracy, but accept popular rule as central rather than constrained by liberal limits.

direct-votes.rationale: Dieterich calls for referendums on major societal questions, and Venezuela's constitution provides four types of citizen-initiated referenda.

workers-councils.rationale: Communal councils and co-management are encouraged but state and elected bodies remain the formal basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Ecuador's constitution calls the state single and indivisible, even while recognizing plurinational autonomy.

natural-rulers.rationale: Egalitarian and indigenous-popular democracy rejects any natural entitlement to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Dieterich's nonviolent transition supports this, but adherents have not been pacifist and Chavez used civil-military language.

war-builds-character.rationale: Adherents condemn wars as imperialist and favor peaceful integration, with no glorification of war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Ecuador's constitution declares a secular state and secular public education, though protecting religious practice.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The constitutions are secular and plural, resting on popular sovereignty and not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The strand opposes privatization and strengthens the state, so private courts and defense are rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Chavez attacked US militarism and the strand favors regional integration over military dominance, though it values defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Plurinational and intercultural state models directly reject a single-ethnicity nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: It draws on Marxian theory and critiques exploitation, though Dieterich's non-class state and Chavez's humanist emphasis soften orthodox class-struggle framing.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Poverty reduction and redistribution aim at substantive equality, but sources speak of equity and equivalence rather than strict equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Ecuador's constitution makes indigenous community lands inalienable, requires consultation on resource projects and allows ancestral territorial districts.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialism and indigenous roots imply it, but sources do not cite reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: The strand favors Latin American unity (ALBA, CELAC) on regional and political grounds, not explicitly shared religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Its social production enterprises privilege solidarity, cooperation and reciprocity over profit, rejecting self-interest as an organizing value.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Ecuador's text pairs duties and rights but frames rights as the primary guarantee, so the answer leans against putting duties first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecuador's constitution gives Pacha Mama the right to integral respect for its existence and to restoration.

limit-population.rationale: The sources do not address it and the strand's focus on poverty and inequality rather than population suggests rejection.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Dieterich blames industrial capitalism, but governments pursued industrial and extractive development while buen vivir criticizes it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Buen vivir stresses community and nature over disruption; inferred, not stated.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Participatory democracy implies human citizen control; inferred, with no explicit statement.

restore-past-order.rationale: The project is explicitly forward-looking and post-capitalist, aiming to build a new society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wilpert shows adherents pragmatic about forms of property but Chavez framed the project as an ideological socialist one.

direct-action.rationale: The approach uses elections, referendums and constituent assemblies to take power, not abstaining from them.

means-match-ends.rationale: Wilpert says 21st-century socialism must be libertarian and participatory, and Dieterich advocates democratic means to reach a democratic end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The project seeks expanded production and welfare under planning and rejects abandoning civilization.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The equivalence economy retains labor-time accounting and specialization; there is no explicit abolition aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Missions provide free health, education and food, and values of solidarity and equity guide enterprises, but Dieterich's economy pays by equivalent labor value.

production-for-use.rationale: Dieterich rejects market-price allocation, and social production enterprises prioritize non-profit values, though profit-seeking private firms persist.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Dieterich bases his model on the Marxian labor theory of value, which treats profit as arising from workers' labor.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The strand explicitly rejects Marxism-Leninism and 20th-century state socialism in favor of democratic, non-violent transition.

collective-farming.rationale: Land reform and cooperatives were promoted, but the sources do not call for collectivizing all agriculture.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Chavez blamed US-led wars and capitalism for global problems, though a theory of inter-imperial war is not elaborated.

taxation-theft.rationale: The model depends on state redistribution to fund social programs, so taxation is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: The constitutions allow limits for collective rights and the common good beyond harm prevention, but this is inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Ecuador's constitution recognizes collective rights of indigenous peoples, communities and nature.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed directly, though the civil-military union integrates the armed forces with the people.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The strand centers participatory voice and voting, and the idea is hostile to its collectivist outlook.

state-as-business.rationale: Post-neoliberalism rejects market logic in public administration.

positive-liberty.rationale: Wilpert says it aims to realize liberty and solidarity with equality, and missions supply material means of health, education and food.

media-academia-power.rationale: Adherents often criticize private media power but the sources do not make this claim about universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: It is egalitarian and anti-racist, with intercultural and indigenous equality at its base.

organic-representation.rationale: Communal councils are local bodies but sit alongside, not replace, parties and elections.

total-state.rationale: Wilpert contrasts it with state socialism and says it should be libertarian and participatory.

national-rebirth.rationale: Chavez's Bolivarian project speaks of national refounding against neoliberalism, but not decadence-based rebirth rhetoric of the nationalist right.

bound-labor.rationale: Ecuador's constitution forbids forced labor and the project's land reform favors those who work the land.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Sources do not address epistemology; adherents' critique of neoliberal ideology and indigenous knowledge suggests partial sympathy.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; buen vivir stresses indigenous cosmovision while humanism claims universal values.

single-common-good.rationale: The model embraces pluralism and minority rights within majority democracy, though it frames politics as serving the popular majority against oligarchy.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Left Bolivarian governments broke or downgraded relations with Israel and backed Palestinians, but the sources do not address it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Ecuador's constitution recognizes Kichwa and Shuar as languages of intercultural relation, supporting indigenous language revival, though not as the state language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Co-management and worker takeover experiments and participatory planning in social production enterprises directly express it.

school-vouchers.rationale: The missions expand public education provision, so vouchers for private schooling run against it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Post-neoliberalism rejects austerity and favors greater government investment.

economic-freedom.rationale: Adherents reject the neoliberal claim, arguing democracy is built through social rights and public control of the economy.

rule-by-example.rationale: Constitutions rely on law and institutions; sources do not endorse rule by moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Sovereignty against the US and regional self-determination are central, with ALBA built to defend it.

force-without-un.rationale: Chavez condemned US-led wars launched outside international consensus.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist-rooted rationalism meets religious and indigenous traditions in the movement.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Missions were open to residents broadly and regional solidarity is stressed, but this is inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Missions provided free health, education and food as rights, not conditional on work.

class-collaboration.rationale: The model targets exploitation and oligarchy, though it pursues gradual transition and cooperatives rather than open class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Ecuador's constitution protects cultural heritage and indigenous knowledge.

dominated-front.rationale: ALBA, SUCRE and CELAC were created as a regional bloc excluding North America and opposing US influence.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Constitutions affirm equality of men and women before the law, though some adherents are socially traditional.

ban-interest.rationale: The strand is not Islamic; it favors state credit and regional currency, not banning interest.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxian root treats the state as class rule, but Dieterich's vision aims at a non-class democratic state used by the majority, so adherents hold both.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Governments in Venezuela, Ecuador and Bolivia financed programs by extractive exports, while buen vivir and Yasuni-ITT oppose extraction.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Intercultural and plurinational outlook rejects forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in the strand's sources, and it contradicts its anti-racist egalitarian outlook.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the strand stresses participatory forms over the electoral formula.

national-mission.rationale: Chavez promoted his model regionally, yet anti-imperialist framing rejects imposing governments on others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Dieterich lists sexism among problems to be overcome, though it is a secondary concern.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: It defines itself against a political and economic oligarchy and corrupt neoliberal elites.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from rights commitments; adherent governments themselves faced such accusations.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Opposes minimal government; a strongly interventionist state is central.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts its intercultural and egalitarian foundations.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Ecuador's constitution sets equality and non-discrimination as basic rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Adherents pursue regional integration and say socialism needs it, but without the orthodox call for revolution elsewhere.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial and indigenous roots suggest it, but the sources do not discuss it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; plurinational legal pluralism pulls the other way for indigenous justice.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Ecuador's constitution protects freedom of religious practice.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No basis in the strand; contradicts its aims.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Ecuador's constitution makes public education secular at all levels.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; adherents who face US hostility strengthen the state, but they do not use this orthodox doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Popular sovereignty, referendums, and recall are central to its democratic claims.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed beyond protectionism; export earnings from extractives were crucial.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: It is not libertarian: it justifies state expropriation and taxation, though it also stresses nonviolent change.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Its enterprise ideal privileges solidarity, cooperation and reciprocity over competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The 1999 constitution protects multi-party politics, but adherent governments pursued restrictions on opponents.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-oligarchy and anti-imperial themes echo freedom from domination, but the sources do not use the republican idea.

separated-powers.rationale: Critics note adherent governments concentrated powers, and the constitutions added extra branches rather than rely on separation as such, so adherents lean against strict checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rejects Leninism in favor of participatory democracy, though Chavista parties stress leadership.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The social missions and redistribution through oil revenue prioritize the poor.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The strand backs worker organization and participation and would not restrict strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Dieterich blames capitalism and neoliberal restructuring, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Plurinational model treats diversity as a constitutional value.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Participatory democracy relies on elections and referendums; lottery is not proposed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The constitutions emphasize rights, although Chavista governments invoked emergency powers, so this is mixed leaning against.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Venezuela used price controls and subsidized food markets, and the 2003 capital controls and state intervention were typical.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 1999 constitution enshrines pluralism, though adherents backed public media and regulated private broadcasters.

party-commands-army.rationale: Wilpert describes a civil-military union within state structure, not party command.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed in sources; adherent parties vary.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Regional integration and solidarity suggest looser citizenship rules; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: It builds supranational regional bodies like ALBA, CELAC and the SUCRE currency, though they exclude the North.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Strong presidential systems prevailed in the adherent countries but it is not a doctrinal point.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; the strand is neutral on church governance.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; an orthodox Leninist stance not adopted by this strand.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Constitutions protect freedom of expression and cultural creation.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Chavez and Morales sought removal of term limits, which supporters defended as popular choice while critics compared it to caudillos.

recall-officials.rationale: Venezuela's constitution provides citizen-initiated referenda including recall, and Ecuador's allows recall of elected authorities.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Ecuador bans foreign military bases and the strand opposes US influence, but the full position is inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; no source calls for banning rentals.

people-in-arms.rationale: Chavez used the Maoist-inspired formula of the military and people united, but does not call to abolish professional armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; indigenous agrarian roots coexist with urban-based support.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The missions expand education and the movement draws on intellectuals, so it is not anti-educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Interculturality and respect for indigenous peoples assert equal dignity of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Ecuador's constitution protects the right to life and abolished capital punishment, and Venezuela's constitution also bans it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Adherent governments differed, with Correa resisting some sex-education reforms, and the sources are silent.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular public education is constitutional in Ecuador and rationalist Marxian roots oppose it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Latin American constitutions typically grant birthright citizenship, and the strand's solidarity is inclusive, but this is inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Ecuador's constitution recognizes indigenous languages and intercultural education.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The 1990s IMF restructuring and debt crises are the movement's founding grievance, and Ecuador audited and defaulted on part of its debt, though sources are brief.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Dieterich's argument is that political democracy without a transformed economy fails, and anti-neoliberal nationalizations aim at real sovereignty.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Venezuela (1999), Ecuador (2008) and Bolivia (2009) all rewrote constitutions through elected constituent assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: It claims democratic legitimacy and gradual change, though critics say its governments narrowed freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Solidarity-based internationalism and anti-neoliberal critique imply obligations of rich countries, though the emphasis is on trade and sovereignty over aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are contrary to its anti-militarist, anti-imperialist platform and none of its governments pursued them.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidents were directly elected in adherent states under their constitutions.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Post-neoliberalism rejects independent technocratic monetary policy in favor of state control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and no doctrine of the strand bears on it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Ecuador's constitution requires property to have a social and environmental function, and Wilpert shows Venezuela subordinating firms to social values.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Chavez warned against repeating the Soviet distortion, treating Soviet socialism as a model to avoid, though adherents do not uniformly use the state-capitalist label.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Rights of nature and buen vivir support precaution, though governments did not consistently apply it.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; regional defense integration exists but no mutual-defense doctrine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and no doctrine of the strand bears on it.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Constitutional secularism exists but no hostility to religious institutions is documented.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Its presidents were openly partisan and led the political project.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ecuador's text calls the state indivisible, but the sources do not address force.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts popular sovereignty and secular republicanism.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Redistribution through progressive taxes and public spending fits the program, and a flat tax runs against it.

workers-nation.rationale: Its anti-imperialism is organized through regional Latin American integration, so workers and peoples are meant to act across borders more than along strictly national lines.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; participatory democracy and accountability pull toward it, but adherent governments did not adopt such a rule.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Bolivarian unity of Latin America is regional rather than a reunification doctrine.

character-from-environment.rationale: Socialist premise that exploitation and social conditions shape people, and that a new society produces new solidaristic citizens; inferred rather than stated in the sources.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Andean constitutions embed rights, recall and participatory checks, and the project presents itself as constitutional and democratic rather than rule by decree.

space-expansion.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the priority on social programs and anti-capitalist critique of elite spending.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The model seeks power with the people through referendums and communal councils, not a blend with elite bodies; inferred from its participatory emphasis.

leader-cult.rationale: Theorists such as Dieterich favour participatory democracy, yet Chavismo built a strong personal cult around Chavez, so adherents are split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Ecuador's constitution makes child-raising a joint responsibility of mothers and fathers in equal proportion; a custody presumption is inferred from this.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Chavez attacked the oligarchy, but the project is gradual and electoral with markets persisting, and the party-restoration claim is a Maoist idea; split.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Bolivarian project redistributed land and Ecuador subordinates property to its social function.

refugee-return.rationale: Left governments of the movement backed refugee and Palestinian causes; inferred, not central.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Regional integration aims at peoples together, not territorial claims on neighbours; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Ecuador's constitution declares a secular state and guarantees freedom of belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Ecuadorian constitution guarantees equality and freedom of belief, so compulsory covering is opposed; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: ALBA's SUCRE regional currency shows the project favours shared currencies among developing countries.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Ecuadorian preamble commits to Latin American integration and the Bolivarian project unites the region's peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The 2008 constitution recognises indigenous peoples' own institutions and a plurinational state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Left indigenous and minority movements in the project seek rights where they live; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Marxist-influenced project stresses structure and class relations, though Dieterich rejects strict determinism; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Ecuador's constitution requires the state to prevent monopolies and oligopolies in the private sector.

no-bailouts.rationale: Anti-neoliberal governments opposed rescuing banks with public money; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Participatory, majoritarian democracy through referendums and communal councils sits against courts blocking the people; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Ecuador's constitution requires gender equity and parity in public selection and in party governing boards.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Ecuador seeks food self-sufficiency, but the project favours regional integration, not closure from trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The Ecuadorian constitution's rights of nature and labor rights fit binding standards in trade agreements; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Equivalence economy rewards labor; no sourced stance on moral versus material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Change is meant to come gradually through elections and constituent assemblies, not armed vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The republican constitution rests on equality and nondiscrimination; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Bolivarian and Andean projects emphasise national and indigenous history and sovereignty in education; inferred from the 2008 Ecuadorian constitution and Chavista practice.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The project is anti-imperialist and rejects domination of poorer peoples by the US or Europe, and the Ecuadorian constitution rejects imperialism and colonialism.

patriotic-education.rationale: Bolivarian education promoted love of the homeland and Bolivar's legacy, with national symbols central to the movement.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Andean constitutions guarantee indigenous and Afro-descendant rights and affirmative measures, so abolishing preferences runs against them.

public-money-creation.rationale: Chavez and Correa curbed central-bank independence and used state banks for finance; the position is inferred, not a stated programme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Dieterich and Chavez argue capitalism cannot be fixed and must be replaced, though the project is gradual and does not expect imminent collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The project opposes imperial influence and seeks regional integration among equals; inferred, as most states involved were colonies.

delink-world-market.rationale: The project favours resource sovereignty and regional alternatives such as ALBA over neoliberal integration, but kept trading oil; only partly delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Dependency-theory framing of rich-country workers sharing imperial profit is common in the Latin American left, but not a central tenet of this strand.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Ecuadorian constitution guarantees equality and prohibits discrimination, and the movement treats it as a violation of rights.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 2008 Ecuadorian constitution enumerates rights that are entrenched and judicially enforceable, though Chavista practice favoured popular majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and the Andean constitutions' stress on sovereignty and indigenous rights; Chavez and Morales condemned colonial borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: Chavista and Andean socialism rely on elections and constituent assemblies and reject monarchy and hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from majoritarian participatory democracy; the strand does not give minorities a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the stress on popular sovereignty and the recall referendum of the Bolivarian constitution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not applicable; the strand is republican with presidents, not monarchs.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The 2008 Ecuador constitution recognises the rights of nature and Pachamama, and buen vivir stresses harmony with nature.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from buen vivir and rights of nature, which stress respect for nature, but the strand did not address animal use and adherents are split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The strand favours state-led redistribution but frames it as justice and solidarity rather than duty of the privileged; adherents are split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Participatory democracy through communal councils and referendums makes active citizenship central.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist and Latin American critique of media; Chavez attacked private media as serving elites.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from the Gramscian idea of hegemony in the Latin American left, with Chavez attacking the media and church hierarchy.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dieterich and Chavez blamed neoliberal global capitalism and the US for Latin American dependency.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the stress on rights of indigenous and plurinational citizens, though Chavez attacked foreign-born influence.

party-own-road.rationale: Chavez pursued a Bolivarian road and rejected Soviet-style models, as Dieterich framed socialism as distinct from the Soviet kind.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Resource nationalization and regional integration aimed at reducing dependence on US loans and the IMF.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred; Bolivia has a standing sea claim on Chile, but the strand did not make it a general principle and adherents are split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The Bolivia and Ecuador constitutions recognise indigenous rights and plurinationalism, and Morales led as an indigenous president.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Chavismo celebrated its own anti-oligarchic politics but anti-fascism as constitutional doctrine is not a theme of the strand.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the left's rejection of equating communism with fascism; Chavez praised Cuba and Marxist movements.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred; the strand follows the left consensus that slavery drove the Civil War and has no stake in revisionism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the strand's removal of colonial monuments, such as Chavez's replacement of the Columbus statue.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; the strand favours equality for women and social programmes but no stance on men's issues, so adherents are split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the left's focus on violence against women, which the 2007 Venezuelan law addressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the strand's stress on distinct Latin American and indigenous forms of democracy and rejection of the Washington Consensus.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred; Chavez was himself a soldier and favoured civil-military union, but the 2008 constitutions give the military a role under civilian authority, so low.

paid-care-work.rationale: The 2008 Ecuador constitution recognises unpaid domestic and care work as productive work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed by the project; Andean communal traditions value family ties but the sources give no stance.

office-by-exam.rationale: The project stresses participatory democracy and election or recall of officials over technocratic selection; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalisation of strategic resources and sectors is a core policy, with state control of oil, mining and utilities.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Ecuadorian constitution's secular state and rights framework; the sources do not address divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Participatory democracy, communal councils and the constitutional recall of officials are central to the project.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The project rejects neoliberalism and privatised social security in favour of state-guaranteed social rights.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The constitution makes property serve a social function and protects communal and indigenous land, and the project favours social property.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Elected legislatures were part of the new constitutions, but Chavez governed with enabling laws and decrees; contested, inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: The Ecuadorian constitution recognises indigenous languages alongside Spanish and the project stresses plurinational rights.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the project's resource nationalism and anti-neoliberal, sovereigntist stance.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's anti-discrimination and affirmative-action provisions for indigenous and Afro-descendant peoples.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Buen vivir is explicitly framed as an alternative to consumerist, growth-driven capitalism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Chavez opposed US-style foreign wars and interference and ALBA stresses sovereignty, though the project has been accused of aiding allies.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-imperialism and sovereignty are central, so a great power invading an ally to keep it in its bloc is rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Dieterich's strand and the Pink Tide governments attack corporate and oligarchic power over the state.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Chavez-era governments restricted foreign funding of NGOs on sovereignty grounds; inferred as the strand's stance.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Never addressed as a programme; adherents are split.

residents-only-property.rationale: Never addressed; communal land rules exist but resident-only purchase is not a stated demand.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 2008 Ecuadorian constitution recognises work as a right and the strand favours state employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: The strand sees Western democracy promotion as a cover for imperial intervention; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Participatory democracy implies obedience to popular law more than to bourgeois law; the strand does not reject a duty to obey outright, so inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Chavez and Correa stressed national sovereignty and rejected outside interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: Pink Tide governments backed labour organising; industry-wide form is inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the strand; its programme is anti-imperialist and class-based rather than minority-targeting. Inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Ecuadorian constitution recognises marriage; abolition is not a stated aim.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Ecuadorian 2008 constitution guarantees access to public information.

local-production.rationale: Food sovereignty and local production are enshrined in the Ecuadorian 2008 constitution.

informal-organisation.rationale: The strand relies on communal councils and parties such as the PSUV; informal-only organising is not its model. Inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The 2008 Ecuadorian constitution limits ceding jurisdiction to international arbitration and stresses sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: The strand is secular and class-based; religion does not define the nation. Inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Chavez and ALBA built anti-US sovereignty-based integration, so ritual submission to a leading power is rejected; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Oil and resource revenue is nationalised and spent through national programs, so keeping it regionally is inferred to be rejected.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Wilpert describes social property alongside private firms and personal property, so the line is inferred to hold.

defeat-communism.rationale: Chavez declared capitalism unable to solve problems and led anti-US politics; inferred opposition to a campaign to defeat communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Free public health and education missions are state-run and Ecuador's constitution makes them state-guaranteed rights.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Ecuadorian constitution makes the state secular and respects indigenous spiritual beliefs, rather than treating religion as an illusion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Chavez said capitalism cannot solve the people's problems, and the project rejects neoliberal capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Left programme of rights and social property implies economic reform for equality; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: A left project of expanded social services is inferred to favour public provision of care work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not a stated concern; indigenous language revitalisation under the Andean constitutions counters purism; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: The Andean constitutions recognise indigenous rights and the project is hostile to rollbacks; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperatives, co-management and communal councils are part of the project, though markets and private firms persist.

majority-settlement.rationale: Indigenous rights and self-determination in the Andean constitutions imply opposition to settlement steered against minorities; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The project is defined as rejecting both neoliberal capitalism and Soviet-style state socialism for a new course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Indigenous territorial rights in the Andean constitutions point one way and anti-imperial sovereignty over existing populations another; mixed.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Nothing in the project supports denial and it is a left human-rights tradition; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The left, anti-discrimination Andean constitutions point this way; inferred, as the sources do not discuss it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The project promises change through elections, referendums, recall and constituent assemblies with participation, not suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Ecuador's constitution establishes a secular state, so punishing blasphemy or other religions is ruled out.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The project is anti-imperialist and anti-neoliberal, and ALBA was founded against US-led domination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not part of the project; inferred disagreement from its secular state and anti-intervention outlook.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A secular state is established in the Andean constitutions and legitimacy comes from elections, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Dieterich's participatory democracy, communal councils and co-management are defining features.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Indigenous rights, anti-racism and class struggle are linked in the Andean constitutions; inferred rather than stated.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Left-wing Andean constitutions bar discrimination, but the project says little on gender identity; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: The project says nothing on assisted dying and leaders are Catholic or secular left; no common line.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The project is explicitly socialist and a left alternative to capitalism, not a blend of left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Chavez says capitalism cannot solve the people's problems and the project seeks co-management; inferred link to alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The project is anti-imperialist and egalitarian; inferred, as the sources never discuss it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Ecuador's constitution and the project vest authority in the people, through referendums, recall and constituent assemblies.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The state is secular, though no religious-dress ban tradition is documented; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A pro-worker project; inferred, as the sources do not discuss it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wilpert says markets persist alongside social property and social programmes, but the project also nationalises strategic sectors.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Chavez and ALBA treat national defence and sovereignty as central; inferred disagreement.

rich-first.rationale: The project is egalitarian and rejects neoliberal trickle-down; its missions aim to include the poor first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: ALBA, CELAC and SUCRE exclude North America and oppose US blocs, but Venezuela also allied with Russia and Iran; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The project works through elections, referendums and constituent assemblies, and Ecuador's constitution sets up elected offices, so hereditary succession is incompatible with it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the stress on cooperatives, social property and a popular and solidarity economy over profit-making banking; the sources do not describe user-owned credit specifically.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The project defines itself against neoliberal capitalism and the US-led order, and Chavez and Correa broke with the IMF and lenders' conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Participatory democracy and universal suffrage are central, as in Ecuador's constitution, so wealth qualifications are rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Andean constitutions' rights of nature and gender equality; the explicit link between the two dominations is not in the sources.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-derived critique of capitalism and Dieterich's equivalence economy, which aims to replace market value with labour-based value.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from Chavez's long conflict with the privately owned media and the demand for popular, community media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Constitutions and enabling laws coexist: the project stresses constitutional order, but Chavez governed by decree under enabling laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Ecuador's plurinational constitution and Bolivia's indigenous-rights programme are inclusive and reject ethnic limits on citizenship.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on participatory democracy; the sources do not mention internet platforms.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the stress on participation and social control of public bodies; transparency of records is not discussed in detail.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the secular, pluralist, inclusive stance of the Andean constitutions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the inclusive stance of the Andean constitutions.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Participatory democracy through referendums, communal councils and constituent assemblies is central, and Ecuador's 2008 constitution builds in citizen participation, but randomly selected assemblies were not the model used.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the project was largely silent on religious doctrine and was split, with Chavez invoking a social Christ and Correa and Morales drawing on Catholic and indigenous traditions.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Opposition to capitalist concentration of wealth and social ownership of strategic resources are core to the project.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Ecuador's 2008 constitution bars discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, which implies equal treatment in public service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Andean constitutions define a secular state that guarantees freedom of belief, and Chavez framed socialism with Christian language, so promoting atheism is foreign to it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the project's reliance on state security and justice institutions alongside communal councils; abolitionism is not part of it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the majoritarian, plebiscitary model of popular power, though the Andean constitutions add plurinational recognition of indigenous peoples.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The movement answers poverty with state-run missions and guaranteed social rights rather than charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the leaders' push to allow indefinite re-election, which fits the idea of a continuing revolutionary project.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: participatory democracy relies on referendums, recall and communal councils, not standing proxy delegation of votes by policy area.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources do not address extinction risk; buen vivir and rights of nature point to environmental concern but not a top priority on this specific risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's gender equality principles; religious institutions are outside the project's concern.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ecuador's constitution guarantees equal rights and duties of spouses in marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from its participatory democracy and inclusive stance; not directly stated in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from its state role in housing and the social-rights emphasis of the Ecuadorian constitution.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not directly addressed in the sources; inferred as split between opposition to monopolies and acceptance of state innovation.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its participatory civilian model; militarised youth drilling is not part of the programme.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialist and peace-oriented stance and the Ecuadorian constitution's pacifist provisions.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The 2008 Ecuadorian constitution prohibits foreign military bases, consistent with the strand's regional anti-US integration.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the strand; no documented position.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its stated aim of an economy serving labour through cooperatives and co-management rather than capital.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from its state-centred, electoral approach, which does not espouse absolute pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed; the strand stresses plurinational and indigenous identities rather than a single ancient continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by the strand; adherents are split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the strand; adherents are split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Chavismo honours independence heroes but the strand has no doctrine of sanctifying martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from its secular, materialist socialist framing of politics.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by the strand; no documented position.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from its state-led constituent-assembly route to change, which puts political and economic transformation first.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The 2008 Ecuadorian constitution is plurinational and protects indigenous and minority rights, rejecting majority-group economic dominance.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from its plurinational model, which keeps existing territorial divisions while granting indigenous autonomy.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the stress on participatory democracy and popular organisation; Venezuelan practice often tied unions to the movement, so adherents are not uniform.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Socialism of the 21st century is defined by protagonist participatory democracy and worker and communal power, as Wilpert describes.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public provision of health, water and services is central; Ecuador's constitution declares water and health public goods and the Bolivarian missions fund local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Ecuador and Bolivia kept bicameral or unicameral arrangements variously, and the sources do not show a settled position.

municipal-property.rationale: Social property is meant to include cooperatives and co-management alongside state and private firms, but the sources emphasise the national state and nationalised resources rather than local ownership alone.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the communal councils and communes model that federates local assemblies, though practice was run from the centre.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional emphasis on just remuneration enough for a dignified life; Ecuador's constitution guarantees fair pay for workers and their families.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Never addressed; adherents emphasise universal state health provision rather than regulatory speed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Never addressed in the sources and not a priority of the movement.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from state control of strategic sectors and anti-capital-flight exchange controls in Venezuela.

online-anonymity.rationale: Never addressed; the movement's governments both supported and restricted media and online speech.

person-over-state.rationale: Wilpert describes the project as putting the collective and social needs ahead of individual interests; the human being is meant to be the end, but the community and state are given priority in practice.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Buen vivir and indigenous cosmovisions have spiritual elements, but the secular Marxist-influenced core is silent on the claim.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Ecuador's and Bolivia's constitutions entrench autonomy rights for indigenous territories and regions, which is inconsistent with free revocation; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Ecuador's 2008 constitution restricts genetically modified seeds and declares the country free of GM crops, as the primary text shows.

dense-cities.rationale: Never addressed; buen vivir and rights of nature favour environmental concerns but no urban form position is stated.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement rejects race as a basis of politics though indigenous rights are central; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Indigenous pride and plurinational identity are affirmed in the constitutions but racial pride as phrased is not discussed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialism of the project; Ecuador's constitution renounces aggression and foreign bases, but armed forces for regional defence were embraced.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: the Andean constitutions are plurinational, recognising several nations and languages within one state, though regional integration appeals to shared Latin American identity.

communal-electorates.rationale: Ecuador's 2008 constitution establishes a secular state, and the project's participatory democracy runs through common civic bodies.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: Chavez and allies routinely described US-backed plots against their governments, including separatist movements, though partition is not central.

free-public-college.rationale: Ecuador's constitution and Bolivarian missions expand free public education, in line with the project's rights-based social programmes.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Rights of nature favour environmental protection, but the project is oil-funded and no polluter-pays taxation is documented.

future-generations.rationale: Buen vivir and the rights of nature in Ecuador's constitution express a duty to preserve the environment for coming generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The constitutions stress gender equality but the sources do not claim women bring distinct values to politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Chavez opposed US wars and favoured regional peace, but his governments also built up their armed forces.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: the project's participatory-democracy ideal and criticism of US-dominated diplomacy favour transparency, though not documented.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: Bolivarian governments used exchange controls to protect national resources and sovereignty, in keeping with rejection of neoliberalism.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the project's state-led, constitutional path to change; Chavez nonetheless armed civilian militias and communal defence, so adherents are not uniform.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from Chavez's nationalist, anti-US stance and Bolivarian army-people unity; the sources discuss opposition to US wars but not conscientious refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Worker participation, co-management and strong unions are part of the Bolivarian vision of economic democracy, though sources do not centre on bargaining rules.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; the model favours direct missions and social property over tax-system top-ups, so a tax credit is neither central nor opposed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Post-neoliberal governments rejected IMF-style austerity and rules constraining social spending; Chavez declared capitalism could not solve the people's problems.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: ALBA and regional integration were built explicitly against the FTAA and the US-led economic order to favour developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Change is meant to come through elections and constituent assemblies that rewrite the state's constitution, not by a Leninist smashing of the existing state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Wilpert describes a mix of state, co-managed, cooperative and private property with markets persisting, without a fixed blueprint, though adherents still aim at socialism.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Ecuador's constitution gives nature rights of its own and buen vivir rejects reducing nature to a priced asset, although resources are treated as state wealth.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from a civic, plurinational, secular-state outlook in the Ecuadorian constitution; patriotic Bolivarian rhetoric exists but the nation is not framed as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from free-education and anti-neoliberal commitments; student loan debt is not discussed in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from indigenous-rights and anti-exploitation framing in the Andean constitutions; the sources do not use the internal-colonialism concept directly.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; humanist dignity and rights appear in the constitution, but the project says nothing on fixed human nature or its redesign.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from state support for community and public media, but Chavista governments controlled state broadcasters rather than keeping them independent.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred: the project is secular in economics and its Andean constitutions are plural and secular, with no stated doctrine on religious truth, and adherents range from liberation theology to atheism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Post-neoliberal governments backed peasants and cooperatives with state credit and purchasing; the sources do not detail crop price floors, so inferred from this state-led, cooperative approach.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: Latin American left governments sit in a nuclear-free region and Ecuador's constitution bars foreign military bases and favours peace, but nuclear arms were never a theme.

workers-own-party.rationale: Chavez built the PSUV as a mass socialist party and the project stresses popular protagonism, though it is framed as a broad popular movement rather than a class-only party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the Ecuadorian constitution's rights guarantees and bar on discrimination; the issue was not a theme and indigenous custom claims complicate it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Ecuador's constitution guarantees equality and non-discrimination and women's access to property, and the project's social-justice framing supports equal rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address language classification, and the Andean constitutions emphasise respect for indigenous languages and names.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The project favours state regulation, social control of property and constitutional rights of nature enforced by the state, which is the opposite of leaving pollution to private lawsuits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: Ecuador's constitution recognises indigenous authorities and their law within their territories, but Bolivarian participatory democracy works through elected councils and assemblies, not an advisory chiefs' body.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from buen vivir, rights of nature and the social function of property, which subordinate private use to collective and ecological ends, though oil-funded extraction qualified this in practice.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: the Ecuadorian constitution stresses rehabilitation and rights of the accused, and the project has no stated doctrine of fixed sentences.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; the project's internationalist regional integration and plurinational Andean states make a language duty unlikely to be a priority, but nothing opposes it either.

missingStatements.text: Basic natural resources such as oil, gas and minerals should belong to the nation and be used to fund social programs.
missingStatements.rationale: Nationalization of gas, mining and oil and oil-funded missions are central, and Ecuador's constitution calls nonrenewable resources inalienable state assets.

missingStatements.text: Free-trade blocs with rich countries should be replaced by regional integration among developing countries.
missingStatements.rationale: ALBA was founded against the Free Trade Area of the Americas and CELAC and the SUCRE currency exclude North America.

missingStatements.text: Nature should have legal rights of its own.
missingStatements.rationale: Ecuador's constitution gives Pacha Mama a right to integral respect and restoration.

notes: Strands differ: Dieterich stresses an equivalence economy and gradualism, Chavez and later Chavismo a more state-led and personalist model, and Andean versions an indigenous buen vivir emphasis. Social-issue positions (abortion, same-sex marriage, drugs) split adherents. Many answers are inferred from principle and marked low or medium.
